info.title: Zendiloos API
info.description: Management API of the Zendiloos NAS operating system.

get.summary: All accounts, ordered by name.

post.summary: Creates an account with its Linux user and SMB password.

delete.summary: Deletes another account with its Linux user. Its files stay.

patch.summary:
Changes another account's full name, role or whether it is enabled.
Disabling ends its sessions and SMB access.

post.summary:
Sets a new password for another account, which must change it at its
next login. Ends its sessions.

get.summary: Every app of every catalog, by name. Needs `containers.manage`.

One app of a catalog, with what it needs from the NAS. Needs
`containers.manage`.

The app's icon, a PNG checked when it was fetched. Needs
`containers.manage`.

Whether apps can run: Docker installed, its data on a pool. Needs
`containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Puts Docker's data (images, containers) on a pool; Docker restarts.
Needs `containers.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: Docker missing, or its data on another pool

post.summary:
Installs Docker from Debian (`docker.io`, `docker-compose`) and puts
its data on a pool, as a job; apps can be installed afterwards. Needs
`containers.manage`.

get.summary:
The installed apps, with what Docker makes of them. Needs
`containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Installs an app from a catalog: its data and Docker's on the same pool,
an account of its own, access to the shares picked; the agent checks it
against the catalog's policy before anything runs. Needs
`containers.manage`.

get.summary: One installed app. Needs `containers.manage`.

delete.summary:
Removes an app with its containers, images and data, then its access
to shares and its account, as a job. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary: The last lines its containers wrote. Needs `containers.manage`.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: The last this many lines, 1 to 5000; 200 if left out.

post.summary:
Installs a failed app again, with its values. Needs
`containers.manage`.
Starts an installed app's containers. Needs `containers.manage`.
Stops an installed app's containers. Needs `containers.manage`.

Brings an app to the version its catalog offers now, keeping its
values. Needs `containers.manage`.

404.description: `not_found`: the app or its catalog entry

422.description: `invalid_app_value`: the new version needs a value

get.summary:
The catalogs apps come from: the community catalog first. Needs
`containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Adds a catalog. It must answer with an index this version reads; its
apps are not reviewed by the community catalog. Needs
`containers.manage`.
Fetches every catalog again. Needs `containers.manage`.

delete.summary:
Removes a catalog; the community catalog stays. Needs
`containers.manage`.

post.summary: Signs in with name and password.

200.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set.

post.summary: Ends the current session.

204.description: Signed out; the session cookie is removed.

post.summary: Changes the caller's password and ends their other sessions.

get.summary: The signed-in account and the CSRF token of this session.

post.summary:
Reads a Compose file as Compose would and names what it lets
containers do beyond themselves. Needs `containers.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: Compose cannot read it, in its words

get.summary: Every container, by name, with its newest use. Needs `containers.manage`.

delete.summary: Removes a container that does not run. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary: The last lines a container wrote. Needs `containers.manage`.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: At most 10 000; 500 if absent.

post.summary: Starts, stops or restarts a container. Needs `containers.manage`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: `start`, `stop` or `restart`

get.summary:
Where Docker's data is, and the pools it could go to. Needs
`containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Moves Docker's data to another pool, in a job: every container stops
meanwhile. Needs `containers.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: too little space, or not on a pool zendiloOS made

get.summary: Every image, the newest first. Needs `containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Removes every image no container uses; says what was freed. Needs
`containers.manage`.
Fetches an image, in a job. Needs `containers.manage`.

delete.summary: Removes an image no container uses. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary: Every network, Docker's own first. Needs `containers.manage`.

post.summary: Creates a bridge network. Needs `containers.manage`.

delete.summary: Removes a network no container is in. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary: The engine at a glance. Needs `containers.manage`.

The shares the caller may put a project's folder in. Needs
`containers.manage`.
Every Compose project, by name. Needs `containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Makes a project: writes its Compose file into the folder, with the
caller's permissions, and deploys it if asked. Needs `containers.manage`.

409.description: `project_exists`; `refused`: Compose cannot read it; `compose_risks`: not accepted

get.summary: One project. Needs `containers.manage`.

delete.summary:
Removes a project's containers and networks, in a job; images, data and
its folder stay. Not for an app of a catalog. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary:
A project's Compose files. Not for an app of a catalog: they hold its
generated settings. Needs `containers.manage`.

put.summary:
Writes a project's changed Compose file and deploys it again, in a job.
Only for a project made here. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary: The last lines of the project's containers. Needs `containers.manage`.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: At most 10 000; 500 if absent.

post.summary:
Fetches the images anew and recreates what changed, in a job. Not for
an app of a catalog. Needs `containers.manage`.

409.description: `app_project`; `project_unconfirmed`: made before what was confirmed was kept, save its file once

post.summary:
Starts, stops or restarts a project's containers. Needs
`containers.manage`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: `start`, `stop` or `restart`

get.summary:
The newest look for newer images, `null` before the first. Needs
`containers.manage`.

post.summary:
Updates every project with a newer image, in a job; `job` is `null` if
there is none. Apps of catalogs are the App Center's. Needs
`containers.manage`.
Asks the registries now. Needs `containers.manage`.

get.summary: When newer images are looked for and taken. Needs `containers.manage`.

What the containers used, sample by sample, oldest first. Needs
`containers.manage`.

parameters.name: seconds
parameters.description: How far back, at most twelve hours; one hour if absent.

parameters.name: containers
parameters.description: Container names, comma separated; all if absent.

get.summary: Which file services run. Needs `system.view`.

put.summary:
Turns SMB and NFS on or off and sets the workgroup and the oldest SMB
version; applied with the shares at once. Needs `system.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: the host did not accept it; the previous settings apply

get.summary:
The signed-in account's favourite folders, in shares it may use.
Needs `files.read`.

put.summary: Replaces the signed-in account's favourite folders. Needs `files.read`.

404.description: `not_found`: a share the account may not use

get.summary:
The signed-in user's personal folder, if they have one, then the
shares whose rules let them in. Needs `files.read`.

Downloads a folder with everything in it as a tar archive, which
Windows, macOS and Linux open without extra software. Refused if
anything inside cannot be read; the share's recycle bins are left out.
Its length is known ahead, so one that breaks off shows as a failed
download. Needs `files.read`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative to the share's root, e.g. `photos/2024`; empty for the root.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: In this snapshot of the share, read only (its label).

422.description: `invalid_operation`: not a folder, too many files

post.summary:
Moves entries into the user's recycle bin if the share has one, deletes
them for good otherwise (and inside the recycle bin), as a job. Needs
`files.write`.

get.summary:
Downloads a file, as an attachment unless a harmless kind is asked for
`inline`. One byte range (`Range`) can be asked for, to resume a
download (`If-Range` with the `Last-Modified` given) or seek in a video.
Needs `files.read`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative to the share's root, e.g. `photos/2024/beach.jpg`.

parameters.name: inline
parameters.description:
Let the browser show the file, if it is a picture, sound, video or
plain text; anything else is saved regardless.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: From this snapshot of the share (its label).

416.description: The range starts beyond the end.

get.summary: A folder's contents. Needs `files.read`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative to the share's root, e.g. `photos/2024`; empty for the root.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: In this snapshot of the share, read only (its label).

404.description: `not_found`: no such share, or not shared with the user, or no such folder

post.summary: Creates a folder. Needs `files.write`.
Renames a file or folder. Needs `files.write`.

Moves entries out of the user's recycle bin back to where they were
deleted from; folders on the way are made again, and a taken name gets
a free one beside it. Stops at the first that fails. Needs `files.write`.

get.summary:
The share's snapshots, newest first: what it looked like then. Needs
`files.read`.

post.summary:
Copies entries out of a snapshot back into the share, each into the
folder it was in; a name that is taken gets `name (2).ext`, so nothing
is replaced. As a job. Needs `files.write`.

Copies or moves entries into a folder, possibly of another share, as a
job. A copy whose name is taken gets a free one, `name (2).ext`; a move
fails. Needs `files.write`.

Uploads a file: the request body, unchanged, any size the volume has
room for. Written under a hidden name and renamed when complete. Needs
`files.write`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The folder, relative to the share's root; empty for the root.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The new file's name.

parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: Replace a file of that name.

get.summary: All groups, ordered by name.

post.summary: Creates a group with its Linux group.

delete.summary: Deletes a group with its Linux group.

patch.summary: Changes a group's description or members.

get.summary: Liveness check for monitoring and the reverse proxy.
get.description:
Public, so it deliberately reveals nothing about the system, not even the
software version.

get.summary: Where the personal folders are and who has one. Needs `users.manage`.

put.summary: Turns personal folders on, on a pool, or off. Needs `users.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: e.g. a share is called home

put.summary:
Gives an account a personal folder, changes its quota or takes it away
(its files stay). Needs `users.manage`.

get.summary:
The most recent jobs, newest first. Changes arrive on the WebSocket
topic `jobs`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most 200; 50 if absent.

get.summary: One job.
A page of the audit log: who did what, newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most 500; 200 if absent.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: `older` of the previous page.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only entries of this action, such as `identity.login`.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Only entries whose action starts so, such as `containers.`.

get.summary: A page of the system journal, newest first.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Which view; `system` if absent.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: This priority and everything more severe; `info` if absent.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most 500; 200 if absent.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: `older` of the previous page, for the entries before it.

get.summary:
Interfaces, addresses, default routes and name servers. Needs
`system.view`.

post.summary: Keeps the change that waits for confirmation. Needs `system.manage`.

put.summary:
Applies new settings to an interface at once. Unless they are confirmed
within two minutes (`POST /network/confirm`, from the new address if
it changed), the old settings return by themselves. Needs
`system.manage`.

409.description: `change_pending`, or `refused`: not managed by systemd-networkd, no such interface

get.summary:
Whether the network can be changed here, and a change waiting to be
confirmed. Needs `system.view`.

The channels notifications go out on, besides the interface. Needs
`system.manage`.

post.summary: Adds a channel: email over SMTP, or a webhook. Needs `system.manage`.

put.summary:
Changes a channel; without `password`, a stored mail password stays.
Needs `system.manage`.

post.summary:
Sends a test message now and waits for the outcome. Needs
`system.manage`.

get.summary:
The most recent notifications, newest first, as the signed-in account
left them: what it cleared away is gone, what it read is marked. New ones
arrive on the WebSocket topic `notifications`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most 200; 50 if absent.

post.summary:
Clears the caller's notifications up to `up_to` away; other accounts
still see them.
Marks the caller's notifications up to `up_to` as read, in every browser.

get.summary:
The rules for new passwords; every account may read them. Never
common passwords or ones containing the account name, whatever is set.

put.summary:
Sets the rules for new passwords; passwords already set stay. Needs
`users.manage`.

get.summary: The signed-in account's interface preferences, the same in every browser.

put.summary: Replaces the signed-in account's interface preferences.

422.description: `invalid_input`: no such wallpaper name or layout

get.summary: The blocks in force, the newest first. Needs `system.manage`.

post.summary:
Blocks an address or network until the block is lifted. Needs
`system.manage`.

409.description: `own_address`: the caller would be blocked; `address_allowed`: it is never blocked

get.summary:
The sessions of every account that have not ended, the most recently
active first. Needs `system.manage`.

delete.summary:
Ends a session; its browser is signed out with its next request. Needs
`system.manage`.

get.summary:
When sessions end, when accounts lock and addresses are blocked. Needs
`system.manage`.

put.summary:
Sets them; counts of failed attempts start anew where a limit changed,
blocks in place stay. Needs `system.manage`.

post.summary: Lifts a block. Needs `system.manage`.

get.summary: Whether the initial setup is still pending.

post.summary: Creates the first administrator and signs them in.

200.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set.

get.summary: All shares, ordered by name. Needs `shares.manage`.

post.summary:
Creates a share: a dataset on the volume with its permissions, offered
over SMB (and NFS, if clients are given). Needs `shares.manage`.

get.summary:
Every share with an account's or group's rule and what it may do.
Needs `shares.manage`.

put.summary:
Sets an account's or group's rules on several shares at once. Each
share that changes gets its permissions at once and its existing files
in a job. Needs `shares.manage`.

patch.summary:
Changes a share. New permissions apply to the share at once and to its
existing files in a job. Needs `shares.manage`.

post.summary:
Stops offering the share and destroys it with all its files. Answers
with the job. Needs `shares.manage`.

get.summary:
The share's snapshots, newest first, and its schedules. Needs
`shares.manage`.

post.summary:
Takes a snapshot now. Schedules never delete one taken by hand. Needs
`shares.manage`.

put.summary:
Replaces how often the share is snapshotted and how many to keep, one
schedule per frequency. Snapshots of a schedule that is removed stay
until deleted by hand. Needs `shares.manage`.

post.summary:
Deletes one snapshot; the share's data stays as it is. Needs
`shares.manage`.

Returns the share to a snapshot: everything changed since is lost, and
so are the snapshots taken after it. Needs `shares.manage` and the
share's name as confirmation.

get.summary: The software RAID arrays. Needs `storage.view`.
All disks of the host. Needs `storage.view`.

post.summary:
Has the disk test itself; its SMART report shows the progress and then
the result. Needs `storage.manage`.

409.description: `refused`: no SMART, or the disk sleeps

post.summary: Stops the disk's running self-test. Needs `storage.manage`.

get.summary:
SMART data of one disk. Sleeping disks are not woken: their report has
status `standby`. Needs `storage.view`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Kernel name of the disk, e.g. `sda`

get.summary:
Every concern about pools and disks in one place, the worst first.
SMART verdicts are the monitor's last ones (read every six hours), so
this reads no disk. Needs `storage.view`.

The ZFS pools. Fails if ZFS is unavailable, e.g. when its kernel module
could not be built for a new kernel. Needs `storage.view`.

post.summary:
Creates the pool of a plan, erasing its disks. The disks are checked
again first: if anything changed since the plan, nothing happens.
Answers with the job. Needs `storage.manage`.

Plans a new pool: which disks would be erased and what the pool would
offer. Erases nothing. Needs `storage.manage`.

Destroys a pool zendiloOS created and erases its disks. All its data is
lost. Refused while shares, apps, the personal folders or Docker's data
live on it (`pool_in_use`, the detail names them). Answers with the job.
Needs `storage.manage`.

409.description: `pool_not_managed`; `pool_in_use`: the detail names what lives on it

post.summary:
Carries out a planned replacement; ZFS then resilvers onto the new disk.
Answers with the job. Needs `storage.manage`.

Plans replacing a device of a pool with another disk. Erases nothing.
Needs `storage.manage`.

Starts checking all data of the pool; progress shows in the pool.
Needs `storage.manage`.

Stops the pool's scrub; what it checked so far stays checked. A resilver
cannot be stopped. Needs `storage.manage`.

get.summary: When the disks test themselves. Needs `storage.view`.

put.summary:
Replaces the self-test plans; a kind without a plan is not tested on a
schedule. A long test runs weekly at most. Needs `storage.manage`.

get.summary: The data volumes. Needs `storage.view`.
Facts about the host and the installed Zendiloos version.

What the dashboard's charts show before live samples arrive over the
WebSocket (topic `metrics`).

post.summary: Reboots or powers off the system. Needs `system.manage`.

get.summary: The SSH server. Needs `system.view`.

put.summary:
Turns the SSH server on or off and sets its port and rules; open
sessions stay. Needs `system.manage`.

409.description: `not_installed`: there is no SSH server; `port_in_use`: another program listens on the port

422.description: `invalid_input`: a port below 1024 or in use, a time to turn off out of range

get.summary: The time zone and how the clock is kept. Needs `system.view`.

put.summary:
Sets the time zone and the time servers, or the time itself when none
keep it. Needs `system.manage`.

422.description: `invalid_input`: an unknown zone, a bad server, a time with servers on

get.summary: The oldest TLS version the web interface accepts. Needs `system.manage`.

put.summary: Sets it; connections already open stay. Needs `system.manage`.

get.summary:
What there is to update, what is going on and how the NAS looks for
updates. Needs `system.manage`.

post.summary:
Installs what the last check found: Debian's packages, then zendiloOS,
whose interface restarts on the way. A restart of the NAS is asked for
separately. Needs `system.manage`.

Looks for a newer release and for Debian's updates, in the background;
the overview says when it is done. Needs `system.manage`.

put.summary:
Which releases are offered and whether the NAS looks daily. Needs
`system.manage`.

name.description: Login name, also the Linux and SMB user name.

password_change_required.description: The account must choose a new password at its next login.

password_changed_at.description: When its password was last set, in Unix seconds.

AccountHome.description: An account with a personal folder.

quota_bytes.description: How much it may store there; absent: as much as the pool has.

ActiveSession.description: A session of some account that has not ended.

address.description:
A GitHub repository (`github.com/owner/repository`) or the https
address of an `index.json`.
An IP address or a network such as `198.51.100.0/24`.

text.description: Each line with the container's name and a timestamp, oldest first.

docker_socket.description: The Docker socket: control over every container, so over the NAS.

generate.description: zendiloOS makes it up; nobody is asked.

length.description: How many characters a generated value has.

official.description:
The community catalog: built in. Apps of other catalogs are not
reviewed by it.

refresh_error.description: Why that fetch failed; the apps read before stay listed.

refreshed_at.description: The last time its index was fetched, in Unix seconds.

skipped.description: Apps left out because they fail the format or the policy.

AppTexts.description: Name and tagline in another language.

AppUpdate.description: A newer state of an installed app.

version.description: The version its catalog names, if it names one.

AppVolume.description: A pool apps can keep Docker's data on.

AppWebAddress.description: Where the app's web interface is, on the NAS's own address.

device.description: Kernel name of the disk or partition.

older.description: Pass as `before` for the next, older page; absent at the end.

actor.description: Account name; for failed logins the name that was tried.

AutoBlock.description: Addresses that fail too often are blocked.

AvailableRelease.description: A newer release of zendiloOS on the channel.

BlockedAddress.description: An address or network the web interface refuses.

automatic.description: Blocked after failed logins, not by an administrator.

until.description: Unix seconds; `null`: until lifted by hand.

CatalogApp.description: An app as the store lists it.

permissions.description: Exceptions from the policy, confirmed when installing.

translations.description: By ISO 639-1 language; English is the default.

version.description: The app's own version, if its catalog names one.

compose.description: The Compose file as written; zendiloOS fills in the variables.

CatalogAppDetail.description: Everything about an app before installing it.

password.description:
The mail password. Left out when changing a channel: the stored one
stays; empty: none.

ChannelLevel.description: The least serious notifications a channel carries.

share_id.description:
For a new project: the share and the folder in it. Without, the
existing project's folder.

risks.description:
To be confirmed before it runs; empty if nothing reaches beyond the
containers.

ComposeRisk.description: Something a service may do beyond its container.

detail.description: The path, namespace, devices or capabilities.

Concern.description:
Something wrong with a pool or disk, as a code with parameters for the
interface to word, e.g. `pool_degraded` with `pool` and `state`.

password.description:
Initial password; the account must change it at its first login,
unless `password_locked`.

path.description: The new folder, relative to the share's root.

pool.description: The pool (volume) to create it on.

oneOf.description: Absent: no quota, lz4, 128 KiB records.

password_change_required.description: Nothing but changing the password is allowed until this is false.

password_locked.description: Only administrators set this account's password.

permissions.description:
Everything this account may do, e.g. `system.view`. The interface
uses it to show only what is allowed; the server checks anyway.

pool.description: The pool to move Docker's data to.

id_link.description:
Name of the disk's `/dev/disk/by-id` link; disks without one cannot
be used for pools.

name.description: Kernel name, e.g. `sda`; identifies the disk in this API.

DiskUsage.description: What a disk is used for.

oneOf.description: The newest sample, while it runs.
`null`: not on a pool zendiloOS made; it cannot be moved here.

used_by.description: The containers made from it, by name.

built_in.description: Docker's own: it cannot be removed.

containers.description: The containers in it now, by name.

cpu_share.description: Of the machine's processors, 0 to 100; `null` before the first sample.

app.description: For an app: its id in the App Center.

files.description:
Where its Compose file is: on the machine for every kind, and in the
share for one made here (`docker/teslamate/compose.yaml`).

DockerSetup.description: Whether apps can run on this NAS.

version.description: The engine's version, while it runs.

oneOf.description: Where Docker's data is, if zendiloOS put it on a pool.

FailureLimit.description: So many failed logins within so many minutes.

path.description: Relative to the share's root; empty for the share itself.

FileServices.description:
Which file services run, and how Samba presents itself; one set for
all shares. Fields added later have defaults, as a fresh install has
them.

bonjour.description: Macs find the NAS and its Time Machine share (Bonjour).

delete_veto_files.description: Folders holding only such files can be deleted.

durable_handles.description:
Open files survive a short network loss; SMB's locks then no longer
hold against NFS or the file manager.

follow_symlinks.description: Symbolic links inside a share are followed; never out of it.

hide_unreadable.description: Shares a user may not open are not listed to them.

mac_compat.description:
Names with characters Windows does not allow, and Apple's
extensions; needed for Time Machine.

multichannel.description: SMB 3 over several connections at once.

nfs.description: NFS for Linux and other Unix systems.

oplocks.description: Clients may cache files they have open.

smb.description: SMB for Windows, macOS and Linux.

veto_files.description: Names kept out of the shares, e.g. `/*.tmp/Thumbs.db/`.

workgroup.description: The Windows workgroup: 1 to 15 letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

FileShare.description: A share the signed-in user may use, or their personal folder.

home.description: The personal folder of the signed-in user.

id.description: `0` for the personal folder, which only its owner sees.

recycle_bin.description: Deleted entries go to `.recycle/<user>` in the share.

FileSnapshot.description: A snapshot of a share, as the file manager shows it.

label.description: Pass as `snapshot` to look into it.

Finding.description: A reason behind the health verdict.

threshold.description: The limit `value` is compared with, for `nvme_spare_low`.

value.description: The count or percentage the finding is about.

path.description: The folder, relative to the share's root; empty for the root.

truncated.description: Too many entries; the rest is left out.

writable.description: The user may create and delete entries here.

oneOf.description: Absent while personal folders are off.

containers.description: The containers made from it, by name.

reason.description: Why it cannot be told, for `unknown`.

ImageUpdateSchedule.description: When newer images are taken: on these days at this time.

check.description: Registries are asked every six hours.

oneOf.description: `null`: newer images are taken by hand only.

confirm_permissions.description: The administrator confirmed the app's permissions.

pool.description:
The pool the app's data goes on, one of `volumes` of `/apps/docker`;
the one Docker's data is on if absent.

ports.description: Port id → host port; missing ones get their default.

settings.description:
Setting id → value; missing ones get their default. Generated
settings are made by zendiloOS.

shares.description:
Share id → the share picked for it: its name, or a folder in it
(`media/Films`), which the app then mounts instead of the whole
share.

digest.description: Of the version installed; for its icon.

pool.description: The pool its data and Docker's are on.

oneOf.description: `None` while Docker cannot be asked.

shares.description:
Share id → the share it got: its name, or a folder in it
(`media/Films`).

source_id.description: The catalog it came from; it may be gone since.
